newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief eyes Internet impact on phone network.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief eyes Internet impact on phone network.

text.p: The chairman of the Federal Communications Commission Friday urged a high-level industry advisory group to keep an eye on the impact of surging Internet usage on the nation's local telephone network.

The comments followed a Reuter story earlier this week noting that industry experts and analysts agree that exploding Internet usage is bringing the phone system perilously close to gridlock by tying up millions of local phone lines nightly. Usage is climbing at an annual rate of 42 percent.
The gridlock has meant fewer calls going through on the first try, more busy signals and even blocked calls, where puzzled callers hear nothing at all after dialing.

"Questions that have been raised about the impact of Internet usage underscore the importance of this council and its work," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said in a statement, referring to the FCC's council on "network reliability."
"It is vital for the public to know that when questions like this are raised, there is a place to go for answers."

Hundt asked the council whether the FCC or the phone industry needs to take steps to address the situation. The advisory group is made up of high-level representatives from the telecommunications industry, standard-setting organizations and consumer groups.

The council, in a quarterly report, said that no phone carriers have reported an event linked to Internet use that meets the criteria for "reportable outages" -- a network failure that deprives more than 30,000 customers of the ability to make a call for more than 30 minutes.
The group, chaired by Nynex Corp. Chairman Ivan Seidenberg, also agreed that the Internet's present mix of applications and growth does not pose any unusual network-outage hazards.
